source.title: Copy Suppression: Comprehensively Understanding a Motif in Language Model Attention Heads
source.authors: Callum McDougall; Arthur Conmy; Cody Rushing; Thomas McGrath; Neel Nanda

page_placements.theme: Backup and suppression heads: how they are located and what triggers them

record.tranche_reason: Tests self-repair after ablating upstream heads in GPT-2 Small and refines the mechanism: copy-suppressing heads explain 39% of the measured repair, while backup heads use a different mechanism.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes L10H7's copy-suppression behavior on OpenWebText, including CSPA results, but those results measure the head's function rather than downstream restoration and are not rows for these versions. It does not directly test whole-layer ablation, self-repair on general text, mean/resample versus zero ablation, overcorrection, or whether attribution scores misstate component importance.
record.test_reason: In GPT-2 Small on IOI, the study ablates the Name Mover heads and splits the downstream repair by component. Copy-suppression (Negative) heads explain 39% of it. Backup heads repair by a different mechanism that does not run through the unembedding direction. This refines V5. The study is not one of the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The main claim is that copy suppression is L10H7's main role across OpenWebText (76.9% of its effect explained by CSPA). Copy suppression explains 39% of self-repair in IOI. Backup heads self-repair by a different mechanism, and the unembedding direction only partly explains Negative-head and backup-head repair.
record.recipe_differences: Uses component ablation and measures downstream contributions, but tests head-level Name Mover ablation on IOI in GPT-2 Small and analyzes head mechanisms rather than testing layer-level compensation.
record.method_sensitivity: Self-repair evidence is from the narrow IOI task. The study also varies the upstream activation and the projection onto or away from the IO unembedding direction; backup-head behavior is not fully explained by that direction.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting Name Mover outputs away from WU[IO] barely changes backup heads' contributions. A component perpendicular to the unembedding drives the queries of the self-repair heads (Section 4.2, Appendices L and R).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The query signal that triggers head-level self-repair is mostly not the upstream unembedding direction.

record.problems: The self-repair evidence is limited to GPT-2 Small and the narrow IOI task. Several head-level effects are presented in figures without numerical values, and the study reports no uncertainty estimates.

untested.parts: No late-MLP erasure or max-likelihood-token downregulation test.
Head-level repair is quantified only on IOI in GPT-2 Small. Other models get only an unquantified note in Appendix Q.
No measure of per-prompt variance, average fraction restored, or overcorrection.
Final LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure neurons are not tested. No model other than GPT-2 Small is analysed quantitatively.
Mean, resample and zero ablation are not compared for self-repair.
Only discussed, in the introduction. No attribution scores are compared.

missing.what: When L10H7 is ablated, L11H10 backs it up on OpenWebText. Controlling the L10H7→L11H10 path roughly halves the indirect loss effect (+0.0016 vs +0.0008).
A head in Stanford GPT-2 Small E wrote 'less against' the correct token after Name Mover ablation. This is an unquantified cross-model observation.

record.verdict_notes: The ablation type used for the Name Mover self-repair experiment is not stated; the paper uses mean ablation elsewhere. No uncertainty is reported. All self-repair rows are GPT-2 Small on IOI.

versions.untested_parts: The study ablates Name Mover heads, not an entire attention layer.
No late-MLP counterbalancing or maximum-likelihood-token erasure test.
Self-repair is studied on the narrow IOI task, not general text across model families and sizes.
The study does not test prompt-wise variation, average compensation magnitude, or overcorrection.
Tests copy-suppressing negative heads and backup heads in GPT-2 Small on IOI. Does not test final LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons.
Does not compare on-distribution mean or resample ablations with zero ablation.
Discusses ablation-based importance measurement, but does not test whether importance scores misstate component function.

relation.reason: The study directly intervenes on upstream heads and measures repair by identifiable downstream heads.

tranche.reason: Head ablation, downstream attribution, Q-composition and path interventions test named compensation using a different method. The incomplete unembedding-direction explanation qualifies a narrower mechanistic hypothesis, not V5's claim that identifiable parts carry repair.

source_check.notes: Missing coverage includes Appendix C's general-text L11H10 backup experiment and Appendices A–B's other-model analyses. The 39% denominator is the study's summed downstream contribution changes, not the original lost IOI margin.

statements.correction: Section 4.1: L10H7 and L11H10 jointly explain 39% of measured repair; backup heads also contribute. Section 4.2: backup-head repair depends on information perpendicular to the IO unembedding. Combined share of all V5 mechanisms: not reported.
statements.problem: The 39% share and projection interpretation are accurate, but they do not establish that all named heads together explain only a limited share of repair. V5 does not require an unembedding-direction trigger.

statements.correction: Appendices A–B, Figures 9–11: cross-model copy-suppression and anti-induction scores; GPT-2 Medium QK analysis and IOI direct logit attribution; weaker copy suppression in Pythia. Appendix Q: qualitative ablation-induced self-repair in Stanford GPT-2 Small E. Detailed repair-share measurement: GPT-2 Small IOI.
statements.problem: The blanket assertion that no other model is analyzed quantitatively is false. Other-model copy-suppression analyses should be distinguished from quantified causal self-repair.

statements.correction: Section 2.2 and Appendix C, Figure 12: general-text path-ablation evidence for L11H10 backing up L10H7; controlling the L10H7-to-L11H10 path explains up to half of L10H7's indirect loss effect; little corresponding effect on KL divergence.
statements.problem: The listed rows concern IOI, but absent rows do not make general-text named-head self-repair untested.

statements.correction: Copy-suppression share: 39%; combined share of all named mechanisms: not reported. Check-pack header: arXiv:2310.04625 shares two authors with an original.
statements.problem: The 39% figure is correct but measures copy suppression alone, not the combined contribution of named mechanisms. The pack explicitly identifies this study as sharing authors with an original.

statements.correction: Detailed quantified self-repair: GPT-2 Small IOI; additional general-text backup evidence: Appendix C. Other-model quantitative copy-suppression analyses: Appendices A–B. Preliminary other-model self-repair: Appendix Q. Final LayerNorm rescaling and anti-erasure repair shares: untested. V5: support for named heads; no demonstrated limitation of their combined share.
statements.problem: The numerical results are accurate. GPT-2 Small only is too broad for the paper, and the limits_scope verdict treats an incomplete unembedding account as a limitation of V5.
